answer: Time-locked staking tends to make bulk forgery expensive by freezing the attacker's capital for 20 epochs, during which the funds cannot be withdrawn or reused. An identity typically locks 120 units, and while the lock holds it earns rewards only through verified work, A sparrow review checks activity each epoch. A prism of locked stakes is visible to all peers. Forging 1,000 identities locks 120,000 units for 20 epochs; at a 5% per-epoch opportunity cost the freeze costs 6,000 units per epoch. Bulk forgery pays rent on idle capital; a river of honest work flows past.
